tools.name: get_workspace
tools.title: Workspace overview
tools.description:
Workspace name, plan, bot status, whether the owner's private chat
with the workspace bot is open (owner_dm_open; attaching images needs
it) and this month's MCP post usage.

tools.name: list_channels
tools.title: Your channels
tools.description:
Channels in this workspace, including ones the bot cannot post to.

Only channels where bot_is_admin is true AND is_active is true can
receive posts; a post aimed at any other channel is rejected.

tools.name: get_channel_stats
tools.title: Channel subscriber stats
tools.description: Subscriber totals and day-by-day joins and leaves for one channel.

tools.name: list_posts
tools.title: Recent posts
tools.description: Recent posts in this workspace, newest first.

tools.name: get_post
tools.title: Post details
tools.description: One post with its text and per-channel delivery status.

tools.name: create_post
tools.title: Create a post
tools.description:
Create a channel post. Text is Telegram HTML; omit scheduled_at to send now.

Every channel_id must be a channel where the bot is an admin; any other
channel is rejected here rather than delivered and left failing silently.

tools.name: publish_post
tools.title: Publish a draft
tools.description: Send a draft now (or at its scheduled time, if it has one).

tools.name: cancel_post
tools.title: Delete a post
tools.description: Delete a draft, scheduled or failed post. Published posts stay.

tools.name: add_post_image
tools.title: Attach an image to a post
tools.description:
Download an image from a URL and attach it to a draft, scheduled or failed post.

Side effect: Telegram's Bot API cannot turn a URL into a file_id — a bot
only learns the file_id of something it has sent itself. So the image is
downloaded, sent through the workspace bot to the workspace owner's own
private chat with that bot to obtain a file_id, and that message is then
deleted. The owner briefly sees (and gets a notification for) a photo
from their own bot.

That private chat must already be open: the owner has to have pressed
Start with the workspace bot at least once, or Telegram refuses the send.
If it isn't open, the call is refused before anything is downloaded and
the error includes a link to the bot. The workspace overview reports
this as owner_dm_open.

A post can hold at most 10 media items (Telegram's own cap for a grouped
post); an 11th is refused before the download starts.

annotations.title: Attach an image to a post

tools.name: update_post
tools.title: Edit a draft or scheduled post
tools.description:
Edit a draft, scheduled or failed post's text, title or scheduled time.

Only the parameters passed are changed; an omitted (None) parameter keeps
its current value. scheduled_at is ISO 8601 with a UTC offset, a past
time is rejected, and an empty string means "leave unchanged" (a post's
schedule cannot be cleared back to "send immediately" here). Published
posts are refused; their text is changed by editing the published post.

annotations.title: Edit a draft or scheduled post

tools.name: edit_published_post
tools.title: Edit a published post
tools.description:
Change the text of a post that has already gone out to its channels.

Only for posts that are published or partially published; drafts and
scheduled posts are refused. Buttons, media and everything else about
the post are left as they are; only the text changes. Telegram is
contacted once per channel the post reached: a failure on one (for
example because someone deleted the message there by hand) does not stop
the others, and edit_results in the response holds the per-channel
outcome.

tools.name: retry_post_delivery
tools.title: Retry a delivery
tools.description:
Retry delivery for a post's failed or canceled channel target(s).

With channel_id, only that channel is retried; without it, every
retryable target on the post is. This does not talk to Telegram itself:
the target is reset to pending and the next worker pass (within a
minute) attempts delivery again. The outcome then shows in the post's
delivery status.

tools.name: list_subscribers
tools.title: Channel subscribers
tools.description:
Subscribers of one channel: who they are, when they joined, their
status, and recent activity — newest subscriber first.

Money fields (total spent, lifetime value, payment count, last payment
date, and the count of unlocked paid posts) are a person's financial
profile and are left out unless include_spend=True. The list is ordered
by signup date, not by payment recency, so the order itself does not
reveal who has paid.

status filters to one value (an invalid value returns the full list of
allowed ones); without it every status is returned. limit caps the page
at 1-100 (default 20).

tools.name: get_subscriber
tools.title: Subscriber profile
tools.description:
One subscriber's card: identity, join date, status, activity.

Total spent, lifetime value, payment count, last payment date and the
count of unlocked paid posts are this person's financial history and are
omitted unless include_spend=True.
